title: How ePBS made it into Glamsterdam
intro: In 2022 it was a philosophy: let the protocol, not a trusted middleman, connect the people who build blocks with the people who propose them. This is how that idea, enshrined proposer-builder separation (ePBS, EIP-7732), became the headline of the Glamsterdam upgrade, with block-level access lists (EIP-7928) beside it. It draws on talks, research posts, client-team notes and forum posts.

stops.author: potuz
stops.source_title: EIP-7732 the case for inclusion in Glamsterdam
stops.note: The champion's headliner proposal: what ePBS buys, and the two objections he says he kept hearing, with his answers.

lines.text: Secondary benefits include the removal of trust assumptions on block productions, allowing any validator to be a builder and bid for block production, without the need to be gated by relays.

Objections that I have received to the EIP have been varied throughout the last two years but have mostly settled in two: - It changes forkchoice. - Builders need to be staked. The first one is a minor change to allow for empty blocks, it minimally changes forkchoice relying on current mechanisms to protect builders. As for the second one I have approached current builders and they have expressed that this it not an important problem for them.

stops.author: Prysm team
stops.note: A consensus client team backs ePBS over the 6-second-slot alternative (EIP-7782): bandwidth is the bottleneck. Date: the HackMD page shows no date, so 15 Jul 2025 is its createTime (checked 6 Nov 2026) and the date on its screenshots.

lines.text: Today, we allocate a mere 2 seconds of each 12-second slot to the critical work of block and blob propagation.

While shorter slots improve UX, they represent a shortsighted optimization that sacrifices long-term scalability for immediate gratification. EIP-7782 only reduces overhead from ⅔ to ½ of slot time. Meanwhile, EIP-7732's slot restructuring minimizes overhead far more effectively, enabling both higher gas limits and more blobs within existing 12-second slots.

stops.title: Chosen for Glamsterdam
stops.body: Core developers scheduled ePBS (EIP-7732) for the upgrade then called Amsterdam, now Glamsterdam. A week later, on All Core Devs Execution #218 (14 August 2025), block-level access lists (EIP-7928) were confirmed as its execution-layer headliner.
stops.note: Not in our catalogue; we link to Forkcast and never copy it. Confirmed from the call transcript and the Glamsterdam meta EIP (EIP-7773). On #162 Alex Stokes only proposed ePBS and block-level access lists as the two headliners while the execution-layer side was conditional; Tim Beiko confirmed both on All Core Devs Execution #218 (14 Aug 2025, transcript; Forkcast has no key-decision file for #162 or #218).

stops.title: Scheduled, not shipped
stops.body: ePBS (EIP-7732) is scheduled for Glamsterdam, which has not shipped. Forkcast lists the upgrade as upcoming with no activation date set. Call ACDE 248 postponed the Hoodi testnet fork so a security disclosure affecting the repricing EIPs can be analysed, and no new date is set. The block gas limit at the fork was settled after the debate above: ACDE #243 (13 Aug 2026) confirmed 200 million gas for Glamsterdam and ACDE #246 (24 Sep 2026) scheduled it at the fork on Sepolia (Forkcast).
stops.note: Primary source: Forkcast, re-read 6 Nov 2026 (ethereum/forkcast: src/data/eips/7732.json shows Glamsterdam status Scheduled, headliner; src/data/upgrades.ts shows Glamsterdam status Upcoming, activationDate TBD; src/components/network-upgrade/OverviewSection.tsx says ACDE 248 postponed the Oct 26 Hoodi fork to analyse a security disclosure affecting the repricing EIPs, no new date). The earlier tagline 'Rollout paused while a security disclosure is analyzed' is no longer on the page, so it is not repeated. The disclosure is described by Forkcast as affecting the repricing EIPs, not ePBS. EF Protocol's 7 Sep 2026 post says December 2026 and Justin Drake said January 2027 at Devcon 8, so no date is stated here.
